subject.title: Feature: support message read action for Telegram

question: Should the bundled Telegram plugin expose observed-only message reads, and if so what retention, default enablement, and authorization contract should govern the stored chat content?
rationale: Source inspection establishes the implementation gap, but repository policy cannot choose whether bundled Telegram should retain group content or how broadly agents may query it; those choices alter privacy and security behavior.

options.title: Approve bounded observed-only reads
options.body: Add an explicit action gate and bounded SQLite-backed store containing only messages the running bot observed, with documented retention and access semantics.

options.title: Provide a generic hook only
options.body: Prioritize the passive inbound hook represented by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/83101 and leave archival and history querying to separately installed plugins.

options.title: Decline retained history
options.body: Keep Telegram transport stateless beyond existing operational context and document that the Bot API cannot provide arbitrary chat-history reads.

recommendation.title: Approve bounded observed-only reads
recommendation.body: Add an explicit action gate and bounded SQLite-backed store containing only messages the running bot observed, with documented retention and access semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: The existing issue review already frames the unresolved product, privacy, and Telegram API choices, making this the strongest available routing signal.
